meta_description: Dubai all-inclusive hotels from €205 to €1,523 a night for two, plus the one hotel that truly bans children, compared on board, beach, score and room size.

lead: For an all-inclusive in Dubai, book Amwaj Rotana on JBR at €270 a night for two: beach 100 steps away, a 42 m² sea-view room and all meals for just €84 more than room-only. The cheapest all-inclusive is Towers Rotana at €205 (city, metro opposite), the cheapest on a beach is Riu at €207, and for a spa splurge it's The Retreat Palm at €376.

The catch: only one hotel here actually bans children, voco Dubai Monaco at €134 (half board €271), and it has no all-inclusive rate. Many hotels tagged adults-only still welcome kids under their house rules. All 10 were compared on the all-inclusive and room-only price for the same night, child policy, beach and pools, room size and guest score. Filter by beach, adults only, couples, families or budget below, or jump to the comparison table.

review: Amwaj Rotana is the all-inclusive to look at first in Dubai. For €270 a night for two you get a newly renovated 42 m² sea-view room with a balcony, the beach about 100 steps away and The Walk at JBR outside the door. The same room costs €186 room-only, so all your meals for two add €84 a night, the smallest jump on this page after Towers Rotana.

It also has the best position of the beach options: a 9.5 location score, a tram stop three minutes away, Jumeirah Lake Towers metro nearby and a free mall shuttle. That matters on an all-inclusive, because the hotel's three restaurants (Horizon, Benihana and Rosso) are only part of what is on your doorstep.

Compared with Sheraton The Walk (#4, €273) nearby, Amwaj is €3 cheaper, sits closer to the sand and scores higher on location; the Sheraton has slightly bigger rooms (45 m²) and lets pets stay. Compared with Riu (#3, €207), you pay €63 more for a 5★ hotel, a bigger room and a far better location.

The catch: this is a family-friendly hotel, with a children's pool and slide and the Splashpad water park five minutes away. If kids at breakfast would spoil it, look at voco Dubai Monaco (#2). Taxes and charges are added to the €270.

review: If “adults-only” is the non-negotiable part of your search, this is the hotel. voco Dubai Monaco is the only property in this comparison whose house rules say children are not allowed: minimum check-in age 18, no cots, no extra beds. Plenty of Dubai hotels carry an adults-only tag and still welcome children of any age; this one does not.

It also has the lowest headline price here: €134 a night for two for a 36 m² sea-view room with a balcony over the pool, on Europe Island at The Heart of Europe. What it does not have is an all-inclusive rate. The closest is breakfast and dinner for €271, which is about what Amwaj Rotana (#1) charges for full all-inclusive.

The biggest catch is the curfew: entry to the property is closed between 22:00 and 07:30, and check-in also stops at 22:00. That rules out dinner cruises, late flights in and nights out in the city. It is built for slow beach days, two restaurants (French and Mediterranean) and the spa.
On top of the price come a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and an AED 20 tourism fee per night. An AED 500 damage deposit is taken by card on arrival and refunded within 7 days.

review: Riu is the only place on this page that is an all-inclusive resort first and a hotel second, and it is the cheapest way to get one on a beach: €207 a night for two. That covers a 30 m² Double Room with a balcony, four restaurants (the Al-Ándalus buffet plus Asian, Italian and Lebanese à la carte), a private beach area and four pools.
For €10 more you get a partial sea view (€217) and for €20 more a full sea view (€227), worth it because the base room looks onto the garden. The 56 m² Junior Suite with sea view is €311.

The trade-off is position. Riu sits on Deira Islands with a location score of 8.2, the lowest here, so plan on taxis for Downtown or the Marina. And it is a family resort, with a waterpark, slides, kids' pool and playground, so couples after quiet should look at voco Dubai Monaco (#2) or The Retreat Palm (#5).
Against Towers Rotana (#6, €205), Riu costs €2 more but gives you the beach and four restaurants instead of a city-centre tower and a metro stop. The €207 excludes taxes and charges.

review: Sheraton The Walk is the hotel to book if you are unsure whether all-inclusive is worth it, because it prices every board on the same room. The 45 m² Deluxe Room costs €126 room-only (non-refundable), €150 with breakfast, €211 with breakfast and dinner, €245 with all three meals and €273 all-inclusive.

Read that ladder and the decision gets easy. Going from full board to all-inclusive costs only €28 a night for two, while going from breakfast to all-inclusive costs €123. If you eat out most nights on The Walk, the €150 breakfast rate is the smart buy; if you will drink by the pool, all-inclusive is.

Against Amwaj Rotana (#1, €270), it is €3 more for a 45 m² room instead of 42 m², a 4★ rating instead of 5★ and a slightly lower location score (9.2 vs 9.5). In its favour: pets are allowed, and Fogueira's 15 cuts of meat and shisha lounge are one of the better in-house dinners on JBR.
On top of the price come a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and an AED 15 tourism fee per night.

review: The Retreat Palm is the all-inclusive for couples who want quiet more than a scene. It sits on the beach of the Eastern Crescent of Palm Jumeirah, calls itself the Middle East's first wellness resort, and puts the Rayya Wellness centre (cryotherapy, facials, hammam) at the centre of the stay.

All-inclusive is €376 a night for two in a 35 m² Deluxe Room with a balcony. The resort prices five boards on that room, and the useful one to notice is full board at €319: the step from there to all-inclusive is €57. From room-only (€202) the all-inclusive premium is €174, one of the biggest jumps on this page.

Against the W (#7, €471) a few minutes up the coast, it is €95 cheaper and much calmer; against Amwaj Rotana (#1, €270) you pay €106 more for the Palm setting and the spa, but get a smaller room. For more resorts on the Palm, see our Palm Jumeirah hotels comparison.
On top of the price come a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and an AED 20 tourism fee per night. It is not adults-only: children are welcome and there is a kids' pool.

review: Towers Rotana is the cheapest all-inclusive we found in Dubai: €205 a night for two in a 40 m² newly designed room on Sheikh Zayed Road. The same room is €163 room-only, so all-inclusive adds just €42 a night for two people, the smallest premium on the page.

This is a city hotel, not a resort. The food is Flavours on Two (buffets with theme nights), Long's Bar (a British pub), a poolside snack bar and 24-hour in-room dining. The pool is on the roof, with a sauna, steam room and hot tub. What you get instead of a beach is position: opposite Financial Centre Metro, 5 minutes from Dubai Mall, and a free shuttle to Kite Beach.

Against Riu (#3, €207), you trade the beach and four restaurants for the metro, Downtown and a better location score (9.3 vs 8.2). Against Al Bandar Arjaan (#9, €214), you get a hotel room instead of a 75 m² apartment, but a far more central address.
On top of the price come a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and an AED 15 tourism fee per night. Bring cash for the AED 500 damage deposit.

review: The W is the all-inclusive for couples who still want to go out without leaving the hotel. It has seven restaurants and bars, from ATTIKO and Ginger Moon to Fish Beach Taverna, an infinity pool facing Palm Jumeirah and live entertainment, and it scores the best comfort of the beach hotels here (9.3).

The price is €471 a night for two, all-inclusive, in a 53 m² room with a harbour-view balcony. That is €184 more than the €287 breakfast rate and €114 more than half board (€357). If you will eat at a different restaurant each night anyway, half board is the stronger deal.

Compared with its neighbour, the Westin (#8, €508), the W is €37 cheaper, aimed at couples rather than families and has bigger rooms (53 vs 52 m²). The beach is 400 m from the hotel according to its description, while the Westin has its own 500 m stretch.
On top of the price come a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and an AED 20 tourism fee per night.

review: The Westin is on this page for one reason: it is the best all-inclusive for families. Room guests get free access to the Jungle Bay waterpark, there is a 500 m private beach, five pools, a kids' club and daily beach games, and ten restaurants and bars, including Barasti.

It is also the most expensive beach all-inclusive here, at €508 a night for two in a 52 m² skyline-view room. Room-only is €285, so all-inclusive adds €223 a night, the largest premium on the page. Half board (€394) is the obvious middle ground with this many restaurants nearby.

If you are searching for adults-only, this is the hotel to avoid: everything is built around children. Couples get a better deal next door at the W (#7, €471), or a calmer one at The Retreat Palm (#5, €376). For more beachfront options, see our best beach resorts in Dubai.
On top of the price come a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and an AED 20 tourism fee per night.

review: Al Bandar Arjaan is the space pick: €214 a night all-inclusive for a 75 m² one-bedroom apartment with a separate living room, two bathrooms and a kitchenette. Nothing else on the page gets close for the price; the next all-inclusive rooms in the same bracket are 30 m² (Riu) and 40 m² (Towers Rotana).

It is a hotel-apartment building connected to the five-star Al Bandar Rotana, so you share its five venues (Salt & Pepper, Gusto, Morgan's Gastropub, Vanilla Lobby Lounge and The Deck Pool Lounge) and a terrace looking over the creek. The pool is on the roof with a bar and skyline views.

The catch is location. This is the north shore of Dubai Creek, with a location score of 8.5 and no beach. It suits families, longer stays and anyone flying in and out of Dubai International, which is minutes away by road. Want the creek's dhow cruises at night? See our dinner cruises comparison.
On top of the price come a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and an AED 20 tourism fee per night.

guide.h2: Dubai All-Inclusive and Adults-Only Hotels Compared
guide.html:
All prices are for two adults on the same January weeknight, before the service charge and taxes. Amwaj Rotana, Riu, Towers Rotana and Al Bandar Arjaan were Black Friday deal rates that night, and Al Marmoom's €1,523 is a members' price after a free sign-in. All-inclusive/night is the all-inclusive rate; room-only from is the cheapest rate for two in the same room type without meals, and the AI premium is the difference, i.e. what all your meals cost the two of you per night.

What the premium tells you: all-inclusive is a bargain at Towers Rotana (+€42) and Amwaj Rotana (+€84), roughly €21–42 per person a day. At the Westin (+€223) and the W (+€184 over breakfast) you are paying €92–112 per person a day for food and drink, which only pays off if you rarely leave the resort. The median all-inclusive price across the nine hotels that offer one is €273.

guide.h2: Adults-Only in Dubai: What the House Rules Actually Say
guide.html:
Dubai has very few hotels that keep children out. Many properties carry an adults only tag in search filters, yet their own house rules say “children of any age are welcome”; the tag often means only that the minimum check-in age is 18. We checked the child policy of every hotel in this comparison, and of the long list behind it.

  • Truly adults-only: #2 voco Dubai Monaco. Children are not allowed, no cots or extra beds, minimum check-in age 18.
  • Adult-leaning but kids welcome: #7 W (nightlife, pets allowed) and #5 The Retreat Palm (wellness, quiet), though both accept children and The Retreat has a kids' pool.
  • Family resorts: #8 Westin (kids' club, waterpark), #3 Riu (waterpark, playground) and #1 Amwaj (kids' pool with slide).

No hotel we found is both adults-only and all-inclusive. The nearest thing is voco Dubai Monaco on half board at €271, or an adult-leaning all-inclusive like The Retreat Palm.

• All-inclusive, best all-round: #1 Amwaj Rotana, €270. Beach 100 steps away, tram 3 minutes, and meals for only €84 over room-only.
  • No children, full stop: #2 voco Dubai Monaco, from €134 (half board €271), if a 22:00 curfew suits you.
  • Cheapest beach all-inclusive: #3 Riu, €207, a classic resort with four restaurants.
  • Cheapest all-inclusive overall: #6 Towers Rotana, €205, a city tower opposite the metro.
  • Not sure you need all-inclusive: #4 Sheraton The Walk, where six boards on one room run from €126 to €273.
  • Quiet and spa: #5 The Retreat Palm, €376.
  • Nightlife: #7 W Mina Seyahi, €471.
  • Families: #8 Westin, €508 with a free waterpark, or #9 Al Bandar Arjaan, €214 for a 75 m² apartment.
  • One special night: #10 Al Marmoom Dome, €1,523 member price, a desert dome with its own pool.

Want luxury without the meal plan? Our best luxury hotels in Dubai and Palm Jumeirah hotels comparisons cover the 5★ resorts that sell room-only or breakfast rates.

guide.h2: Booking All-Inclusive in Dubai: Where, Getting Around and Extra Costs
guide.html:
Where to stay

  • JBR (Amwaj Rotana, Sheraton The Walk): the best location scores (9.2–9.5), beach, tram and The Walk's restaurants on foot. Best if you will still eat out some nights.
  • Mina Seyahi and Al Sufouh (W, Westin): big resorts with their own restaurants and beach, where all-inclusive makes most sense.
  • Palm Jumeirah (The Retreat): quieter, 10 minutes by car to the Marina.
  • Deira Islands (Riu) and The Heart of Europe (voco): self-contained beach stays away from the centre.
  • Sheikh Zayed Road and Dubai Creek (Towers Rotana, Al Bandar Arjaan): city hotels, no beach, close to the metro or airport.
  • The desert (Al Marmoom): 36 km from Al Maktoum International.

Getting around

Amwaj Rotana is three minutes' walk from the JBR 2 tram stop, and Towers Rotana is directly opposite Financial Centre Metro. Towers Rotana runs a free shuttle to Kite Beach and Amwaj a free mall shuttle. Elsewhere, plan on taxis: the Westin puts JBR Walk at 5 minutes and Burj Khalifa at 20 minutes by car. Note voco Dubai Monaco's entry is closed 22:00–07:30.

What costs extra

  • Taxes and fees: every price above excludes taxes. Where the rate shows the breakdown, a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and a Dubai tourism fee of AED 15–20 per room per night are added.
  • Deposits: AED 500 at voco Dubai Monaco (card) and Towers Rotana (cash).
  • Extra beds: AED 120–216 a night where offered; voco has none and Riu has none.
  • Nights out: all-inclusive covers the resort only. If you plan a dinner cruise or a desert evening, a breakfast or half-board rate is usually the better buy for those dates.

faqs.q: Are there adults-only all-inclusive hotels in Dubai?
faqs.a: Not among the hotels we compared. The only one whose house rules ban children is voco Dubai Monaco, The Heart of Europe, and it offers breakfast and dinner (€271 for two) rather than all-inclusive. For all-inclusive with a calmer, adult feel, look at The Retreat Palm (€376) or the W Mina Seyahi (€471), both of which still accept children.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest all-inclusive hotel in Dubai?
faqs.a: Towers Rotana on Sheikh Zayed Road, at €205 a night for two on a January weeknight, opposite Financial Centre Metro. The cheapest on a beach is Riu Dubai Beach Resort on Deira Islands at €207. Taxes and the Dubai tourism fee come on top.

faqs.q: How much more does all-inclusive cost than room-only in Dubai?
faqs.a: For two people per night: €42 at Towers Rotana, €84 at Amwaj Rotana, €147 at Sheraton The Walk, €174 at The Retreat Palm and €223 at the Westin Mina Seyahi. At the top end, half board is often the better deal.

faqs.q: Which all-inclusive resorts in Dubai are on the beach?
faqs.a: Amwaj Rotana (beach about 100 steps away), Riu Dubai (private beach area), The Retreat Palm (on the beach, Palm Jumeirah) and the Westin Mina Seyahi (500 m private beach). The W Mina Seyahi has an infinity pool, with Mina Seyahi Beach 400 m away.

faqs.q: Are children allowed at voco Dubai Monaco?
faqs.a: No. Its house rules say children are not allowed, the minimum check-in age is 18 and there are no cots or extra beds. Entry to the property is also closed between 22:00 and 07:30.

faqs.q: Is the Dubai tourism fee included in all-inclusive rates?
faqs.a: No. The all-inclusive prices on this page exclude taxes. Where the rate shows the breakdown, a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and a tourism fee of AED 15–20 per room per night are added at booking or at the hotel.

methodology: We compared Dubai's adults-only and all-inclusive hotels on live prices for the same night (two adults, one night in mid-January), starting from more than 30 properties. We checked every child policy against the hotel's own house rules, kept only hotels that either ban children or sell an all-inclusive rate, and left out bed-space listings and private apartments. That leaves 1 adults-only hotel and 9 all-inclusive hotels, from €205 to €1,523. Each was scored on the all-inclusive price, the room-only price for the same room, guest and location score, room size, beach and pools, and extras such as deposits and tourism fees. Rankings reward the best all-round all-inclusive first, then the clearest pick for each type of traveller.
